recipes.name: Slow Cooker Teriyaki Pork Tenderloin
ingredients_raw: 3 fresh red chile peppers, chopped, or to taste

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Brown tenderloins on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix together chicken broth, teriyaki sauce, and brown sugar in a bowl. Stir in onion, garlic, red chile peppers, and black pepper.

Put browned tenderloins in a slow cooker and cover with teriyaki sauce mixture. Cook on Low for about 4 hours, turning 2 to 3 times during cooking time to ensure even doneness. The internal temperature of tenderloins should reach 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).
Remove tenderloins from the slow cooker and let rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Spoon liquid over slices when serving, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Teriyaki Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: This sweet and spicy teriyaki pork tenderloin slow cooker recipe is mild enough for young kids. Adjust the spice level with more hot peppers to taste.

video.description: Teriyaki flavors and tender pork tenderloin make an easy and elegant main dish in your slow cooker. After browning two tenderloins, place in your cooker along with teriyaki sauce, chicken broth, brown sugar, garlic, red chile pepper, onion and pepper. Serve delicious slices with the sauce spooned over.

review.reviewBody: Cook on low, not high. I followed the recipe to the letter other than the slow cooker temperature setting and it came out wonderfully. Four hours on low is plenty done. I used a roux to make a sauce out of the mixture

SOOOO YUMMY!!!!!!!!!!

I don't brown for as long as they said too. ? I also heard from another reviewer that the juices didn't absorb as well...but then I break all the meat apart and make it like pulled pork.

I like a lot of sauce so I double or triple what's above because I like the sauce to be all around the meat while it's cooking. Or at least half way up the tenderloins. I do constantly spoon the liquid over, but you don't have too - esp if you make more liquid. I really go heavy on the teriyaki sauce! Basically, I used a large mixing bowl and filled it about half way full of stuff!

Cooking time - I was in a hurry the other day, so I cooked on high for three hours, maybe longer - just long enough to where when I took my fork I could tell the meat would shred easily. Then I removed about half of the liquid, and then shredded the meat. I did end up putting some of it back it, cuz like I said, I like sauce and I used enough to coat the meat + a little more. Then I cooked it on low for about an hour - but not too much longer as the meat is SOOO tender by this point. I have cooked it on low for the full 8 hours too, but still waiting to shred the meat until the last hour or so.

Ingredient alterations - the first time I used this, I used honey teriyaki, but just got regular stuff this time, and added 1/4 cup of honey. Also, I don't use fresh red chile pepper but will add touch of red pepper and some creole seasoning. The BEST is Tony Chacherie's original Creole Seasoning

My pork tenders were small in size, and when I checked the internal temp at 1 hour (not 4 hours), they already were overcooked. I pulled them out of the cooker, let them rest for a few minutes, and then thinly sliced them. I tasted the teriyaki sauce mixture before pouring it over the tenders, and I thought it was too sweet for our taste. However, the pork tenders released their juices while cooking, and the sauce mixture turned out delicious. Using a cornstarch slurry, I slightly thickened the sauce, added the pork tender slices back to the pot, and just let them simmer for another 30 minutes to tenderize even more. Fortunately, I was able to get the rest of my meal together in that half hour, and we just had an “earlier” dinner. I used my Instant Pot® for this recipe, starting with browning the pork using the Saute feature on normal, and then switched to the Slow Cook function on low, and ultimately simmering the pork slices on Slow Cook low, as well. Couldn’t find fresh red chile peppers at the grocery store, so I just chopped up a large jalapeño I had in the fridge which worked out fine. Bottom line, this turned out pretty well, and I’d prepare this way again now that I have a better idea on timing.

Making this today again, made it a week ago for the 1st time. Followed the recipe but did add a few things. We love a lot of flavor and garlic! Used tenderloins but rubbed them with 3 Beer Teriyaki Rub seasoning on both sides and browned on all sides in olive oil before putting in slow cooker. Doubled the liquid (low sodium fat free broth) per some reviewers suggestions, as well as brown sugar (was not to sweet for us). Added a tablespoon of Better than Bullion Chicken to the liquid and about 5 large minced cloves of garlic. Only had red pepper flakes so put about 3/4 tsp in with the liquid with a large onion sliced. Poured all on top and cooked on low 4 hours. Came out PERFECT! We didn’t do anything with the leftover sauce. May be a waste but gave the tenderloin great flavor cooking in it for 4 hours. Very tender but not too tender. Served with mashed potatoes and green beans. Will be in our regular rotation for sure!

My pork loin was 4lbs, so I doubled the ingredients. For each chili pepper I used 1 tsp of chili pepper flakes. I took someone's advice of letting it sit in sauce for 1 hr before cooking. Still seemed dry. Sauce needs to be thicker.

This turned out Great!! My wife is trying to gather new recipes You get into Making the same 20 or 30 dishes after 20 years together. I highly recommend this it’s super easy The main thing that was different than posted recipe was cooked on low for 2-3 hours and added red potatoes that were cubed and boiled in water for 15 min before adding to crock pit And she marinated the pork loin over night In teriyaki and minced garlic This is a definite dish to make again
Cook on LOW for 4 hours is important here. Otherwise you'll get a low rating review like the goober who cooked it on high.

Easy, great flavor. We love the onion so I use a whole one. I leave out the chile pepper so it's too spicy for the kids. And I never bother browning the tenderloins, just trim and stick in the crockpot. Meat comes out tender (almost shreds) and moist.

I made this tonight with great family reviews! Cooked for 4 hours and probably could have done 3.5 hours. I did the flipping, used red pepper flakes as a sub, and did a cornstarch slurry for the last half hour in the slow cooker. Will make again!

Very easy recipe to follow. Delicious! I used a 2 1/2 lb tenderloin and double the sauce ingredients. I also added 1/2 can of pineapple tidbits. I cooked on high for 2 1/2 hours til internal temp was 180. I removed the tenderloin and added corn starch to the sauce and boiled to thicken (On stove) Served with rice, sautéed veggies and Thai salad. Great meal.

Wonderful!! I only had a 1.3lb pork tenderloin so I essentially halved everything. I also added 1/2 red bell pepper slices - adding with the onions. Served a top of Quick Coconut Jasmine Rice by TheDailyGourmet from this site and Thai Cucumber Salad. Excellent pairing! I do wish the sauce was thicker and I think I could have made a cornstarch slurry - adding in after I removed the pork - but overall, this was excellent! So glad I made this and would make again! Thanks Teri!
So delicious, I couldn't stop eating it :) My only change was to sub red pepper flakes and Tony Chachere's Creole seasoning for the fresh peppers.
My husband liked it. I didn’t have the peppers it called for so I used red pepper flakes. It was yummy. I served it on rice and a green salad.

It turned out great! Loved this recipe. I followed some good suggestions in other posts. I seared the tenderloin for 5 minutes per side, then put in crockpot and cooked a 1.3 pound tenderloin for 4 hrs on low, fipping every 45 minutes, for 4 hrs. Then sliced the tenderloin and made a cornstarch slurry and put tenderloin back in for half hour more. It is so delicious!

I must have done something wrong the only thing I changed is I added some bell pepper to the sauce but the meat was practically flavorless. Bummer but on the other hand my husband and I have tried cooking any kind of pork for the last 30 plus years and they've all been failures

Really enjoyed this, I read tge others comments and did several things to my roasts. I did thicken the gravy with a cornstarch slurry and I did let the roasts just sit in the juice for 45 minutes before turning on the crockpot. Cooked for less than 4 hours and dis turn them several times. Served with rice and Asian veggies.
